claims.title: Qualified fragment fusion: rebuild cost, sequence purity and the exposed-end obstruction

quoted_fields.interface: Covalent identifier/root attachment, no independent path or persistent nonspecific retention, complete noncovalent stripping, stable competent intended ports, correct leaves and known orientation. Rebuild models additionally supply IID per-node attempts, child destruction/rebuilding, explicit p/f and costs, and size/protocol-independent acceptance when invoking polynomial scaling or the boundary-only DP. Port/hazard/coding models each retain their separate assumptions.
quoted_fields.failure: Connectivity and mass do not certify site, sequence or orientation. Safe completed fragments do not supply a safe fusion reaction. Correct two-end selection probability is not total accepted-product q without a specified reader/false-acceptance law; two-bond bridge success cannot be imported from one-junction rates. The source phrase n-monomer fragments is ambiguous: code uses total new product n, so child-length convention changes the exponent by two. No measured constant long-fragment q, outer-end masking, compatible label removal, integrated device or equal-resource advantage is acquired. Full demo imports absent astra_chemistry_distributed_edge_assembly; no result JSON/replay log supplied.
